players.product: utility T&D grid infrastructure (transmission/substation connectors and hardware up to 765 kV, System Control control houses) and data-center electrical components (Burndy connectors, PCX power skids, 800 V pin & sleeve devices)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: net sales increased 11% year over year, driven by 8% organic growth and acquisitions contributing 3% (DMC Power 'off to a strong start'); adjusted operating profit grew 18% with adjusted operating margins expanding 110 basis points, 'primarily driven by strong volume growth in high-margin businesses'; adjusted EPS up 16%. Repurchased $168 million of shares in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 net sales $1.517 billion (11% growth; 8% organic growth); adj. operating profit $301 million (18% growth); adj. EPS $3.93 (16% increase)

quarterly_data.signal: Segment detail: Utility Solutions net sales grew 11% (organic 7%, acquisitions 3%), with 12% organic growth in the 'larger, higher margin grid infrastructure business' and demand 'broad-based across T&D end markets'; grid automation organic sales declined 7% year over year (meters/AMI weak, expected to return to slight growth in Q2). Utility Solutions adjusted operating profit grew 21% with margins up 190 basis points. Electrical Solutions sales grew 12% (organic 11%) on data center and light industrial strength; adjusted operating profit $93 million (+10%), margin 16.4%.
quarterly_data.figure: Utility Solutions $949 million (11% growth; 12% organic growth in grid infrastructure; grid automation organic sales declined 7%), adj. operating profit $207 million; Electrical Solutions $568 million (12% growth; organic growth of 11%)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center: CFO said Electrical Solutions 'achieved approximately 40% growth in data center markets in the first quarter', driven by balance-of-system components and modular power distribution skids; order activity 'remained robust' as build-out accelerates 'across hyperscaler and colocation customers', so the full-year data center outlook was raised to 'more than 25%'. Roughly half of data center exposure is the long-cycle modular skid business where 'Orders are booked out through the year, and there's little incremental capacity'; on short-cycle book-and-bill products Hubbell is adding capacity every quarter and building inventory.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 40% growth in data center markets in Q1; FY2026 data center outlook raised to more than 25%; skid orders booked out through the year

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 outlook raised (at this date): total sales growth to 8%-11% and organic growth to 6%-9% (about three points price, the rest volume; Q2 metals-driven price actions added about a point), driven by price to offset inflation and 'enhanced visibility to continued demand strength in our T&D and data center end markets'; adjusted EPS raised to $19.30-$19.85; about 20 basis points of margin expansion at the midpoint (utility-weighted, electrical about flattish); at least 90% free cash flow conversion. Utility Solutions now expected to deliver high single-digit organic growth.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 sales growth 8%-11%; organic 6%-9%; adj. EPS $19.30-$19.85; 20 basis point margin expansion

quarterly_data.signal: High-voltage (765 kV) transmission introduced as an emerging growth opportunity driven by load growth: CEO said it is 'largely incremental to existing strength in traditional 345 kV transmission markets', Hubbell has 'won a couple of orders already' and is developing and testing new products with major customers plus capacity expansion. The opportunity 'represents about 7,000 miles of high voltage transmissions' over 10 years, content per mile goes up slightly at 765 kV, Hubbell sources '85%-90% of material' on a transmission line, and it 'can drive a point of growth above' the high-single-digit transmission and substation outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $1.5 billion addressable market over the next 10 years; about 7,000 miles; a point of growth above high single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Orders: CEO said Q1 orders were 'up, you know, over one' and 'closer to 1.2 to start off the quarter', a mix of short-cycle book-and-bill and projects, with T&D orders also up nicely; demand is going into infrastructure, not channel restocking. Distribution demand recovering with the destock behind it, though growing slightly slower than transmission and substation. Grid automation (Aclara) decline narrowing, with a recent 'pretty nice piece of business that's multi-year'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 orders up over one; closer to 1.2 to start off the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: CEO said the DMC Power substation business is 'meeting and even exceeding a little bit our expectations' and growth this year and next is 'perhaps more a function of our ability to get capacity in place because orders are really supporting'; System-Control shows 'very similar dynamics of good demand and need to add capacity'. CapEx is the highest capital priority and 'you should expect to continue to see that elevated'.

Supply chain and pricing: CFO said there are no significant supply constraints ('chips or metals or component parts'); some aluminum sourced from the Middle East was moved to other qualified suppliers after regional disruption with no impact. Metals inflation (copper, aluminum, steel) led to price increases at the beginning of Q2 that 'have been sticking'; tariff changes (Section 232, IEEPA repeal, Section 122) net about neutral for the year. More than 90% of sales are US-exposed and over two-thirds of the portfolio is exposed to data center and utility markets.
quarterly_data.figure: price actions added about a point to full-year price; more than 90% US sales exposure
